about: Per-language definitions for the structure rules; each language reads its extensions from the convention pack its source names. Each value names its published source; a rule a language cannot use is listed under not_applicable with its reason. A language with no measured cutoff for a scored rule does not run that rule until one is measured (docs/structure-languages.md).

python.module: dotted path under structure.import_direction.source_root, prefixed by import_direction.package
python.edges: import and from-import statements, relative levels resolved against the importer's package

typescript.edges: static import and export-from specifiers, import() and require() with a string literal or a template literal without substitutions; relative specifiers resolve against the importer's folder, then tsconfig compilerOptions.paths and baseUrl from the nearest tsconfig.json; a specifier tries the file, the TypeScript source for a .js specifier, the listed extensions and index files; bare package specifiers are third-party and ignored; type-only imports count

go.module: the package: one folder; its import path is the go.mod module path plus the folder relative to go.mod
go.edges: import specs whose path starts with the module path; _test.go files are not part of the graph
go.note: The compiler already rejects import cycles and enforces internal/ visibility; it allows sibling imports, so sibling-isolation and tier direction still apply.

exempt: files below a folder data_folders names, between the file and its code folder: the data already has its own folder
files under a hidden folder (tool state such as .moon/) or a test data folder (the language pack's placement test_data_dirs)

typescript.code_folder: nearest folder holding TypeScript or JavaScript source
exempt: files below a folder data_folders names, between the file and its code folder: the data already has its own folder
files under a hidden folder (tool state such as .moon/) or a test data folder (the language pack's placement test_data_dirs)
a data file a source file in the same folder imports by a relative specifier (a JSON module is part of the code)
tooling fixed files (package.json, tsconfig*.json and the other tooling-pack names)
files below a folder data_folders names, between the file and its code folder: the data already has its own folder
files under a hidden folder (tool state such as .moon/) or a test data folder (the language pack's placement test_data_dirs)
a file a //go:embed pattern in a .go file of the same package matches (embed patterns may not leave the package folder)
files under testdata/, which the go tool ignores

python.top_tier: the package root and the folders directly under it

typescript.entry: files a package.json bin or main field names, when Git tracks them
typescript.top_tier: the folder holding that package.json and the folders directly under it

go.entry: a non-test file declaring package main, except files constrained by //go:build ignore
go.top_tier: the module root, or cmd/<name>/ directly under it

STRUCT.overlapping-responsibilities.unit: source files of one language directly in one folder; units of different languages are never compared

python.definitions: top-level functions and classes, and the methods of top-level classes; docstrings and comments removed

typescript.definitions: top-level function and class declarations, methods of top-level classes, and top-level const or let declarations whose value is an arrow function or function expression, exported or not; comments removed
typescript.source: measured: 64 labelled unit pairs from 4 repositories, leave-one-repository-out held-out precision 6/7

go.definitions: top-level function and method declarations; comments removed
go.source: not yet measured: the rule does not run for Go

typescript.members: sibling TypeScript or JavaScript source files; stems split at _, -, . and lower-to-upper case boundaries
typescript.domain_word_sources: comments and class, interface and type alias names
typescript.source: measured: 28 labelled clusters from 5 repositories with the Python weights, leave-one-repository-out held-out precision 18/23

python.identifiers: bound names at module and class level: functions, classes and assignment, for, with, walrus, type-alias, except-handler and match-as targets; imports and the names functions, lambdas and comprehensions bind excluded

typescript.identifiers: declared names at top level: functions, classes with their methods and fields, interfaces with their members, enums with their members, type aliases with the members of an object type, namespaces, and every name a variable declaration binds (destructuring included); imports excluded

go.identifiers: declared names at package level: the package clause, functions, methods, types with their struct fields and interface methods, constants and variables; imports excluded

RENAME.residue.source: a rename retires the old name in every language file; a name's words split at underscores, case changes and digit runs (guardrails/foundation/source/names.py); no cutoff

go.reason: A Go folder is a package. Moving prefixed files into a folder named for the concept creates a new package, which changes identifier visibility and import paths: a design change, not a placement fix. Go keeps related files in one package, often with a shared prefix.

shell.reason: Shell scripts have no packages, imports or definitions the rules read.

proposers.reason: The candidate proposers (kind-candidates, consumer-candidates, name-pairs) propose only for these languages: the judgments they feed (technical_kind_grouping, consumer_placement, same_thing) were measured on Python cases. Each proposer also reads TypeScript and Go (signals below), which only a measurement asks for, until labelled TypeScript and Go cases measure them.

signals.about: What each candidate proposer reads in each language, with its published source. A measurement asks a proposer for a language by an explicit languages argument (calibration scripts and tests); the subcommands and the rails propose only for proposers.languages.

STRUCT.kind-candidates.files: a source file whose folder's last segment is a technical-kind word (any language), with at least one definition, except the file that stands for its folder

python.definitions: top-level def and class statements: the header up to its colon, and the first docstring line
python.importers: import and from-import statements, resolved to files as Python's import system would

typescript.folder_entry: index files: an import of a folder resolves to its index file
typescript.definitions: top-level function, class, interface, enum and type alias declarations, and const or let declarations whose value is a function, exported or not: the text up to the body, and the first line of the /** doc comment directly above
typescript.file_doc: the comments before the file's first statement
typescript.importers: static import and export-from statements, import() and require() with a string specifier, resolved as the import rules resolve them (relative, then tsconfig paths and baseUrl)

go.folder_entry: none: every file of a Go package declares the package in its package clause, so no file stands for the folder
go.definitions: top-level function, method and type declarations: the text up to the body, and the first line of the doc comment directly above
go.file_doc: the package doc comment directly above the package clause
go.importers: a Go import names a package, not a file: each built file of the folder an import path names (module path plus folder) has that import's importers; a file outside every module imports no repository package

STRUCT.consumer-candidates.program: a file the package runs as a program, that no other file imports, that the repository neither declares as the package's command nor launches by path, and that sits inside a package rather than in a root folder of its own (fixtures, migrations, scripts, tests)

python.package: the nearest folder above the file holding __init__.py, below the repository root; the top package is the outermost folder of that run
python.own_imports: relative imports and imports whose first name is the top package
python.declared_commands: [project.scripts], [project.gui-scripts] and [tool.poetry.scripts] in pyproject.toml, and console_scripts in setup.cfg or setup.py
python.launched_by_path: a string literal in non-test source naming the file by its dotted module name, its path or (inside its top package) its file name
python.description: the first docstring line of the top package's __init__.py

typescript.package: the nearest folder at or above the file holding package.json, the repository root included
typescript.own_imports: imports that resolve to a file inside the package folder
typescript.declared_commands: package.json bin: a path or a map of command names to paths, relative to the package folder
typescript.launched_by_path: a package.json scripts command, or a <script src> of a tracked HTML file, naming the file by its path from the manifest's or page's folder (a leading / is the page's folder); and a string literal in non-test source naming the file by its path or (inside its package) its file name
typescript.package_run_module_reason: Node has no file a package runs as itself, as python -m runs __main__.py; a package's own command is its bin entry, already a declared command.

go.package: the module: the nearest folder at or above the file holding go.mod, the repository root included
go.program: the main_package marker: a built non-test file of package main that declares func main; the other markers only describe the program
go.own_imports: imports whose path is the module path or under it
go.declared_commands: a main package at the module root or in cmd/<name>/: the documented places for a module's commands, which go install installs by their import path
go.command_manifests_reason: go.mod names no commands; a module's commands are its main packages, placed by layout.
go.launched_by_path: a string literal in non-test source naming the file by its path or (inside its module) its file name
go.imported_by: a main package cannot be imported (the go tool rejects importing a program), so a program has no importers
go.package_run_module_reason: Any file of package main declares the command; the go tool runs a package, never one file name.
go.description: the first line of the doc comment above the package clause of the module root's package

typescript.definitions: the shared name readers (name_pair/extract.py): declarations, aliases and import renames

go.definitions: the shared name readers (name_pair/extract.py): package-level declarations and their members
